name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district lean in a heavily Republican state
Fedorchak is an incumbent with a large financial edge
Markets price the race at ~96% Republican
model.rationale: North Dakota's at-large seat sits in an R+18 district, Fedorchak is an incumbent who has outraised Hammer roughly nine to one, and prediction markets give Republicans about a 96% chance. With no competitive polling or ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a sharp national Democratic wave environment would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of R+18. First-term incumbent Julie Fedorchak is running for reelection after winning the seat in 2024, and she holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised about $1.7 million with over $1 million on hand. Democratic challenger Trygve Hammer has raised under $200,000 and has limited cash available.

No public general-election polling or expert race ratings are available, but prediction markets price the race at roughly 96% Republican. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but lack any visible campaign infrastructure. The combination of the district's strong lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes this a Safe Republican race with little realistic path for an upset.
